title: Permutations and Combinations
seo_title: Geometry Permutations and Combinations Worksheets (TEKS G.13A)
standard_text: G.13A develop strategies to use permutations and combinations to solve contextual problems
meta_desc: Free Geometry probability worksheets for Texas TEKS G.13A: the counting principle, permutations, combinations and probability by counting. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Order matters: permutation. Order does not: combination.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Counting principle: multiply the number of choices at each step.
  • Permutation (order matters): nPr = n! ÷ (n − r)!.
  • Combination (order does not matter): nCr = n! ÷ (r!(n − r)!).
  • Probability = favorable outcomes ÷ total outcomes.

Examples

Example

Choose a president and a treasurer from 10 people

order matters

10 × 9

Answer: 90

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding instead of multiplyingMultiply the choices.
Permutation when order does not matterA team of 3 is a combination.
Dividing by the wrong factorialCombinations divide by r!.

items.q: A committee of 4 is chosen at random from 12 people, including Mia and Josiah. What is the probability that both Mia and Josiah are chosen?
items.e: Ways that include both: 10C2 = 45. All committees: 12C4 = 495. 45/495 = 111.
